notes: I matched 63 of the 65 stations to a Findlay row. Two get null, both observers' stations rather than lights: Fair Isle and the Hynish Signal Tower. Findlay never gives one of these stations in more than one row, so extra_rows is empty everywhere. Hoy Sound Low and High share row 303. Pentland Skerries, Isle of May, Girdleness and Pladda each have both their lights in one row. Things to check: (1) North Carr L.V. -> row 263, but Findlay 1887 calls the lightvessel only 'proposed' (no character), while the reports have a Carr Rock lightship reporting in 1885-87. Check what was on station in 1885-86 and where its character should come from. (2) Row 303 Hoy Sound: Findlay's item 1 is the high light and item 2 the low light. If you split the characters per station, take them from the two items and check against the scan. (3) Easily confused pairs, settled by position: Fladda (330, 'Phladda', Scarba Sound) vs Pladda (343, Arran); Isle Ornsay (316, printed 'Oronsay Island', Sleat Sound); Montrose Ness (273) vs Montrose Harbour (274); Girdleness (276) vs Aberdeen (277); Loch Ryan (356) vs Stranraer (357). (4) In the stations table Ushenish's neighbours ('Island Glass < > Monach Island') disagree with Monach Isles' ('Island Ghlais < > Ushenish'). The lists must order these two differently in some year; that doesn't change the match. (5) Sanda is missing from the 1883-84 reports, and Davaar takes map number 106 in 1884. Check the map numbers there. (6) Findlay's name 'WHALSEY SKERRIES' is really Out Skerries (Bound Skerry). Use the printed position (60 25.4 N, 0 44 W), not the name.
